steps.text: This comment defines our invented brightness scale. Zero means dark and one hundred means bright. It is teaching data, not a physical sensor measurement.
Assign ten to brightness. This is the input for this run. Change this value to test a different reading, then run the program again.
The condition checks whether brightness is less than or equal to thirty. Notice that it includes exactly thirty. Compare that with our requirement, which says below thirty.
When the condition is true, this indented line displays Lamp ON. It prints a message; it does not control real hardware.
Else introduces the alternative branch. Python follows this branch when the condition is false.
This indented line displays Lamp OFF when the condition is false. With the draft, exactly thirty follows the other branch. Repair the condition and check all your cases again.
